newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean Red Cross offers aid talks with N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean Red Cross offers aid talks with N.Korea.

text.p: The South Korean Red Cross on Friday offered talks with the North Korean Red Cross on food aid to the famine-threatened nation.

Kang Young-hoon, president of the South Korean Red Cross, proposed the talks for "speedy and smooth" delivery of food and other relief materials to his Northern counterpart, a Red Cross statement said. The message was delivered via a "hot line" linking the two organisations.

On Wednesday, North Korean representatives demanded substantial international assistance at a meeting in New York with South Korean and U.S. diplomats called to hear Pyongyang's answer to a proposal for peace talks.
Seoul and Washington maintain that large-scale aid can only be discussed during four-nation peace talks, also including China.

Religious and other civic groups in South Korea here have pleged to raise about $20 million to ship 110,000 tones of corn to the communist state. The South Korean Red Cross has made several food shipments in recent weeks.

"I think it is desirable for South and North Korean Red Cross officials to meet and directly discuss speedy and smooth delivery of food and materials being sent to you," Kang said in the message. He called for a meeting in the border village of Panmunjom as soon as possible.
